reviewed: all 16 ABI functions (getters, isBlocked, isAuthorizedToBlock, getProxyAdmin/Implementation, changeIGovernor, the four initialize overloads, blockUntil, changeProxyAdmin, upgrade, upgradeAndCall)

findings.decompiled: def initialize(address templateLibrary_, address clonableTokenAddress_, address initialAdmin, uint256 maxGenerationSize_) ... governor = address(templateLibrary_) ... governor = address(clonableTokenAddress_); proxyAdmin = address(initialAdmin); stor103 = maxGenerationSize_
findings.source: initialize(address _owner, address _governor, ProxyAdmin _proxyAdmin, uint256 _firstUnblockDate); initialize(address _governor, ProxyAdmin _proxyAdmin); initialize(address _governor); initialize(uint256 _firstUnblockDate)
findings.issue: Parameter names from unrelated contracts with the same signatures (template library, token addresses, total supply) label the owner, governor, proxy admin and unblock date.
findings.rule: Use the signature database for function names but neutral parameter names unless they come from the contract's own metadata.

findings.decompiled: mem[ceil32(data.length) + 288] = 0x9623609d...; ... call proxyAdmin with: value call.value wei gas gas_remaining args mem[ceil32(data.length) + 288 len _21 - ceil32(data.length) - 288]; _3 = stor0 / 256; stor0 = 257; _5 = not _3
findings.issue: The forwarded upgradeAndCall call stays raw because solc 0.5 pads the bytes tail with a mask; in the initializer, '_3 = stor0 / 256' is read in the arm where it is known to be 0, so isTopLevelCall is printed as 'not _3' instead of 1, and the two Initializable flags stay one uint16 'stor0' read as 'stor0 / 256'.
findings.rule: Decode a call whose argument buffer starts with a known selector even when the last word is masked; fold a value tested in the enclosing condition; split a slot into the byte fields that are read and written separately.

notes: No loops in BlockableUpgradeDelegator, UpgradeDelegator, Blockable, Governed or zos Initializable. The nested initializer modifiers (4-argument initialize calls Governed.initialize(_owner), UpgradeDelegator.initialize, Blockable.initialize, each with its own check) are reproduced in order; notBlocked, the governor checks with their revert strings and blockUntil's threshold check match the source.
summary: All 16 functions reviewed; no loops and the semantics match, including the nested zos initializers. Only small issues: misleading database parameter names on the initialize overloads, a raw upgradeAndCall forward, and an unsplit Initializable slot.
